We tried to comply to the eligibility rules as best as we could in our registration form but we reserve the rights to refuse/stop participation of teams from countries/companies subject to restrictions at any stage of the challenge.

title: Eligibility
text:
Eligibility for Participation
The inscription form already implements, as far as possible, the restrictions for the origin of participating teams.
The restrictions are mainly about teams originating or affilaited to institutions/companies from (non EUROCONTROL (ECTL)) countries subject to sanctions.
Despite the reason for the sanctions, the practical limitation for us is the impossibility to transfer funds to the winners if based in these countries.
A thematic map of target countries is available at https://www.sanctionsmap.eu/.

title: Eligibility
text:
Eligibility for Prize
The winning submissions/solutions will only be eligible for the awards if

the team does NOT releated to sanctioned countries
external datasets are openly accessible/usable and documented.
all source code will be made openly available on GitHub under the GNU GPLv3 license.
(It will then be forked by the Challenge GitHub account for organizational purposes.)
all additional data sets used are openly available under an open source license.
sufficient documentation is provided to understand and reproduce the results.
the solution is original: teams must use their own original solutions. Re-using any existing implementation is only allowed if the original authors grant you the rights to use their solution and if you made significant modifications to the algorithm or model. In particular, simply re-using existing code and rewriting the data input and output mechanism is not sufficient. Adding parameters to the model and modifying filters to match the specific peculiarities of the data, however, can be considered sufficient.

title: PRC Data Challenge 2026
text:
The Performance Review Commission (PRC) with the support of OpenSky Network (OSN) aims at engaging with data scientists to team up and compete to solve a (big-ish) Data Challenge of interest to the wider Aviation community
The 2026 edition of the PRC Data Challenge proposes to predict the taxi-out time of flights from 11 major European airports. The learning dataset will consist of all airport movements for the full year 2025.
Ranking will use Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) for the submitted prediction for the movements in Jan and Jul 2026.
The competition runs from \(1^{st}\) Sep till \(11^{th}\) Oct 2026 23:59:59 CET.
The total prize amount for the first 3 teams is 5000 EUR.
Check the conditions for eligibility for participation & prize and then fill the following team creation request form!

title: Rationale
text:
The choice of predicting taxi-out time for this year’s data challenge is in line with past data challenges goals of providing information to estimate environmental or operational impact. Taxi-out time is generally difficult to obtain and quite difficult to predict.
A model to infer taxi-out can be used in post-ops analysis to characterize constrained operations intervals and measure excess fuel burnt/CO2 production compared to unconstrained status.
The reasons for variability of taxi-out time are various and interlinked. Taxi-out time can depend on airline specific constraints, airport procedures and load, ATFM related reasons.
